facts: ISRO is India’s national space agency.
Aryabhata was India’s first satellite, launched in 1975.
The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle is used to place spacecraft into orbit.
What is GSLV designed to do?
Launch heavier spacecraft to high-energy orbits
The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle is used for heavier payloads.
LVM3 is ISRO’s heavy-lift launch vehicle.
What did Chandrayaan-1 help confirm on the Moon?
Chandrayaan-1 instruments contributed evidence of water/hydroxyl on the Moon.
What was Chandrayaan-2’s orbiter designed to study?
The Chandrayaan-2 orbiter conducts lunar science from orbit.
A safe lunar soft landing and rover operations
Chandrayaan-3 demonstrated soft landing and rover operations on the Moon.
Vikram carried the Pragyan rover to the lunar surface.
Pragyan was the rover deployed from Vikram.
Why was Chandrayaan-3’s landing region notable?
It was at high southern lunar latitude
The landing occurred in the lunar south polar region.
Aditya-L1 is India’s solar observatory mission.
Why is the Sun–Earth L1 region useful for solar observation?
It offers a nearly continuous view of the Sun
A spacecraft near L1 can monitor the Sun with few Earth occultations.
Which planet did the Mars Orbiter Mission study?
India’s Mars Orbiter Mission entered Mars orbit in 2014.
NavIC provides positioning, navigation, and timing services.
What is the INSAT system mainly used for?
INSAT satellites support communications, broadcasting, and weather services.
What are Indian Remote Sensing satellites used for?
Remote sensing satellites collect Earth observation data.
Where is India’s main orbital launch site?
Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota is India’s main launch site.
What does SDSC SHAR refer to?
Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota
SDSC SHAR is ISRO’s primary launch centre.
Why are cryogenic rocket stages useful?
They can provide efficient high-energy propulsion
Cryogenic engines burn very cold propellants such as liquid hydrogen and oxygen.
Why must a satellite move sideways very fast in orbit?
So it continually falls around Earth instead of straight down
Orbital speed balances gravity with forward motion.
What is special about a geostationary satellite?
It appears fixed over one point on the equator
It flies over both poles every hour
A geostationary satellite orbits once per day above the equator.
Why are polar orbits useful for Earth observation?
They can cover most of Earth as the planet rotates
Near-polar satellites can scan broad swaths of Earth over time.
Why send instruments above Earth’s atmosphere?
To observe wavelengths blocked or disturbed by the atmosphere
Space-based instruments can observe the universe without atmospheric interference.
Why are spacecraft tested before launch?
To reduce risk from vibration, vacuum, and temperature extremes
Testing checks whether spacecraft can survive launch and space conditions.
